defects_in_the_restatement.consequence: This is the most likely route by which a reader derives Lemma 4 from Lemma 3 without noticing which side the field equations are on - which is what J-3 turns out to be about.

numbered_statements.title: First fall degree [7]
numbered_statements.summary: First fall degree D_ff of f_1..f_l: minimal positive integer with multipliers g_i such that (1) max deg(g_i f_i) = D_ff, (2) sum != 0, (3) deg(sum) < D_ff, (4) deg(f_i) <= D_ff.
numbered_statements.note: Condition (1) reads '=' here and condition (4) is present. 2015/984's Definition 5 reads '>=' and DROPS condition (4). The divergence is real and is confirmed in both PDFs.

numbered_statements.title: First fall degree Assumption
numbered_statements.summary: The degree bound for F4 Groebner computation of f_1..f_l is D_ff + O(1).
hypotheses: stated as an assumption; the paper notes it has counterexamples and that Petit et al. restrict to general polynomials

numbered_statements.summary: Under Assumption 1, F4 Groebner computation of f_1..f_l costs <= O(N^{D_ff*C+O(1)}) with C ~ 3.
If F = sum_{i=1}^N G_i (X_i^p - X_i) with D := deg F, then there exist G'_1..G'_N with F = sum G'_i (X_i^p - X_i) and deg G'_i <= D - p for every i.
hypotheses: p a small prime or a power of a prime (section 1)
G_1..G_N local polynomials in F_p[X_1..X_N], N = d*n'
F is GIVEN as sum_{i=1}^N G_i (X_i^p - X_i), i.e. F lies in the ideal generated by S_fe
hypotheses_NOT_carried: no monomial order (one is CHOSEN inside the proof)
no reducedness of F or of the G_i
no dependence on Definition 1, Definition 2, or Assumption 1/2
definitions_depended_on: local polynomial / local variable / N = d n' (section 1, pymupdf 71-78)
numbered_statements.proof_technique: descent on psi(G) = max monomial among LM(G_i X_i^p), over the set of all representations, under a GRADED monomial order

numbered_statements.summary: Weight wt(e) = sum of the p-adic digits of e; extended to global monomials additively.

proof_defects_in_lemma_2.what: The case NUM(G) > 1 with deg psi(G) = D falls through both branches.
proof_defects_in_lemma_2.fill: deg psi(G) >= D always; when equal, deg G_i + p <= D for every i and the conclusion is immediate.
proof_defects_in_lemma_2.evidence: recheck.out:57,61 - two of four test tuples terminate in this unhandled case

proof_defects_in_lemma_2.what: The NUM(G)=1 branch asserts D = deg F = deg psi(G) with no argument.
proof_defects_in_lemma_2.fill: psi(G) cannot cancel: against another G_j X_j^p because j not in IND means strictly smaller; against any G_j X_j because a graded order makes those strictly smaller in total degree. One sentence.

proof_defects_in_lemma_2.what: Claim 1) is printed X_{I_1}^p | G_{I_i} - the whole multiplier.
proof_defects_in_lemma_2.fill: Weaken to X_{I_1}^p | LT(G_{I_i}), which is true and is all identity (3) uses.
proof_defects_in_lemma_2.evidence: recheck.out:63-72 - witness p=2, N=2, G=(X+Y^2, Y+X^2): X^2 does not divide Y+X^2 but does divide its leading term

proof_defects_in_lemma_2.fill: Valid and used only for i = 2..k; for i = 1 it would require X_{I_1}^p | LT(G_{I_1}), not guaranteed.

proof_defects_in_lemma_2.what: 'G^new_{I_1} X^p_{I_1} = ... = sum LT(G_{I_i}) X^p_{I_i} = 0' is false as a polynomial identity.
proof_defects_in_lemma_2.fill: What vanishes is the coefficient of psi(G). The correct identity is G^new_{I_1}X^p_{I_1} = (G_{I_1} - LT(G_{I_1}))X^p_{I_1} - sum_{i>=2} LT(G_{I_i})X_{I_i}, every monomial of which is < psi(G).

proof_defects_in_lemma_2.what: Claim 2) prints the same expression on both sides of an equality; the proof writes the ring F_p[X_1..X_d] where the statement says F_p[X_1..X_N].
